Average Wi-Fi or a busy network (the wiki's lower HEVC range)

notes: Starting point compiled from public guidance, NOT verified by the VisionALVR project on this headset (no `verified` entry). VisionALVR's support for headsets other than the Apple Vision Pro is best effort.

Differences from the Apple Vision Pro profile: the Quest 3's panel is 2064 x 2208 per eye (about 2K) against 3552 x 3200 (4K) on the Vision Pro, so the stream is about 2.4x fewer pixels, needs about half the bitrate (100-150 Mbps against 300) and the encoder has an easy job on any NVENC GPU (split encoding is not needed). Same as on the Vision Pro: 90 Hz, HEVC 10-bit (ALVR's Quest client advertises 10-bit HEVC decoding; the default session already forces 10-bit), full colour range, ALVR foveated encoding, chroma-key passthrough on pure green.

ALVR's wiki (Settings tutorial, v20): on a good wireless router use the medium resolution preset (the default) with sharpening 1.0 and HEVC at a constant 100-150 Mbps; HEVC is usually the best codec when bitrate is limited; turn foveated encoding on and tune it from the statistics graph.
Resolution, gamma and the encoder details are left out on purpose: the headset's own default (what ALVR reports at the handshake) is used. Change them in the wizard if you know better.
Panel about 2064 x 2208 per eye (Meta's specification); refresh rates 72/80/90/120 Hz. 90 Hz is the commonly recommended balance, 72 Hz the stable fallback.
ALVR's wiki: AV1 works only on the Quest 3 with an RTX 4000 / RX 7000 or newer GPU. VisionALVR's encoder path is HEVC, so this does not apply here.
